title: Code-review and design-review exercises
objectives: Run a Salesforce code-review exercise on Apex or LWC using tests, bulk-safety, and sharing as first-class comments.
Run a design-review exercise on objects, automation, and access before anyone writes code.
Separate style nits from defects that Well-Architected would call untrusted, unreadable, or unadaptable.
Give review feedback that is evidence-based, not status-based.
diagnostic_question: You are handed a trigger that updates Opportunities in a loop and a design that stores legal comments on a public Opportunity. What defects do you raise in code review versus design review, and what would you not block on?
definition: Code-review and design-review exercises are structured critiques: design review asks whether the data model, sharing, and automation are the right shape; code review asks whether the Apex, LWC, or Flow implementation is safe, tested, and readable. Apex testing docs require unit tests as part of developing Apex; Well-Architected asks whether the result is Trusted, Easy, and Adaptable. Neither review is a taste debate about braces. ([Testing Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing.htm); [Well-Architected](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview); [Developer trail](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/explore-core-salesforce-developer-responsibilities))
why_it_matters: Interviews increasingly put a diff or a whiteboard in front of you. Candidates who only say 'looks good' or who nitpick names while missing SOQL in a loop fail. Design review catches the public legal-comment field before code review polishes its getter.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a building inspection before occupancy. Design review is the occupancy permit: is this the right structure, fire exits (sharing), and wiring (automation)? Code review is the punch list on the unit that was actually built: tests, bulk-safe loops, CRUD/FLS. You do not fail a building for paint color while missing a missing staircase. You also do not skip the permit because the paint is pretty.
deeper_explanation: The Apex Developer Guide's testing chapter describes a testing framework to write unit tests, run them, and obtain coverage results. In a code-review exercise, missing tests on a trigger path are a defect, not a suggestion. ([Testing Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing.htm))

Well-Architected Trusted includes data security; Easy includes readability and maintainability; Adaptable includes separation of concerns. Use those as review lenses with examples, not as slogans. ([Well-Architected](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview))

The developer trail lists engineering practices among developer responsibilities. Code review is that practice in an interview: you must show you can critique, not only write. ([Developer trail](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/explore-core-salesforce-developer-responsibilities))

Which-tool Help still applies in design review: a trigger that stamps a field a before-save Flow could handle is a design smell even if the Apex is pretty. ([Which tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm))
Do not invent coverage percentages or governor numbers in the review; cite current docs or mark Needs verification.

mental_model.analogy: Building inspection: design review is the occupancy permit (structure, exits, wiring); code review is the punch list on what was actually built (tests, bulk-safety, FLS).
useful_mapping: design review → is this the right building
code review → is this unit safely built
tests → smoke detectors that were actually tested
SOQL in a loop → a wiring fire waiting for volume
Well-Architected → inspection codebook, not a slogan poster
where_it_breaks: Software can iterate; buildings cannot be occupancy-permitted weekly—still, do not skip design review because 'we can refactor later' on security.
Paint color can matter for accessibility; rare style nits are still not the first comment.
Flow has no .cls diff; you still design-review it.
Inspection is not a Salesforce product name.

teach_back_prompt: Review a trigger-in-a-loop diff in five comments: two blockers, two questions, one nit. Then say what belongs in design review instead.

review_schedule.prompt: From memory, restate the core terms and one clarifying question you would ask.
Classify four realistic interview signals using this topic's decision table.
Teach the analogy, then name two places it breaks.
Walk one troubleshooting symptom from evidence to next action.
Give a two-minute interview answer without notes, then one follow-up.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Design review first: objects, sharing, which tool. Code review second: tests, bulk-safety, FLS. I block on security and missing tests, not on paint-color naming.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: If you hand me a schema with legal comments on a public Opportunity, I fail design review before I read Apex. If you hand me a trigger with SOQL in a loop and no tests, I fail code review even if the names are pretty. I use Well-Architected as lenses with examples. I ask whether Flow should have done it. I will not invent coverage percents. I give two blockers, questions, and one nit.

terminology.plain: Critique of shape before or beside the diff.
terminology.precise: Objects, relationships, sharing, automation tool choice, and integration contracts—occupancy permit.
terminology.example: Rejecting a public-OWD legal comment field in favor of a private child object.
terminology.non_example: Arguing about whether a variable should be `i` or `idx` on a perfect design.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Architecture review: longer-form cousin; this lesson includes interview-sized slices.
terminology.boundary: Flow and validation belong in design review, not only Apex.

terminology.precise: Apex, LWC, or Flow XML/metadata: tests, bulk operations, CRUD/FLS, error handling, readability.
terminology.example: Blocking a trigger that queries inside a for-loop without tests.
terminology.non_example: Approving 'LGTM' on an empty PR because the author is senior.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Pair programming: a different practice that can still include review comments.
terminology.boundary: Do not quote unofficial coverage numbers.

terminology.plain: A defect that must change before merge or build.
terminology.precise: Security, data loss, bulk failure, or missing tests on a new trigger path.
terminology.example: SOQL inside a loop on Opportunity Line Item inserts.
terminology.non_example: A rename of a well-tested private method.
terminology.boundary: Employers disagree on nit policy; be explicit.

terminology.precise: Naming, comment wording, import order—paint color. Still polite, never the only comment on a dangerous diff.
terminology.example: Prefer `recordIds` over `ids` in a bulk method.
terminology.non_example: Calling missing FLS checks a nit.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Suggestion: optional improvement that is not a blocker.
terminology.boundary: Accessibility naming can be more than a nit—say why.

terminology.precise: Code-review lens: no SOQL/DML in loops; collections; tests that insert more than one row.
terminology.example: Map-based query before the loop; test with 200 LAB_ records if the scenario is trigger volume.
terminology.non_example: A test that inserts one Opportunity and calls the method.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Governor limits: the platform's enforcement; do not invent the numbers here.

terminology.precise: Apex unit tests run in the review, not a promise to 'add tests later' on a trigger.
terminology.example: @IsTest method that asserts Closed Won is blocked for a LAB_ record.
terminology.non_example: Code coverage screenshot with no assertions.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SeeAllData=true: usually a review smell; confirm current testing docs.
terminology.boundary: Coverage without asserts is weak evidence.

terminology.plain: Did the code respect user permissions?
terminology.precise: Code-review security: with sharing, user-mode or stripInaccessible patterns as appropriate—details in later Apex security topics; here you must ask the question.
terminology.example: Noting a without sharing class that exposes legal comments.
terminology.non_example: Assuming triggers always run as god-mode so FLS is irrelevant to review.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: with sharing: record visibility, not the same as FLS.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent API names of new security features; look them up.

terminology.plain: Apex or Flow used where a simpler tool fits.
terminology.precise: Design-review comment pointing at Help: formula, validation, approval, Flow, Apex.
terminology.example: A trigger that only stamps Last_Touched__c = Datetime.now().
terminology.non_example: Apex for a multi-object service with callouts—probably not a smell.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Technical debt: sometimes you keep the trigger; say so honestly.
terminology.boundary: Do not shame teams; ask for the constraint.

when_to_use: When an interview hands you an Apex or LWC diff for a code-review exercise.
When a whiteboard schema needs a design-review exercise before anyone codes.
When you must separate blockers (tests, bulk, FLS) from nits (naming).
When a trigger exists for a job a validation rule or before-save Flow should own.
When Well-Architected Trusted/Easy/Adaptable can be attached to a concrete defect.
when_not_to_use: Do not turn a code-review exercise into a complete rewrite while ignoring the author's intent.
Do not treat missing tests on a new trigger as a nit.
Do not skip design review because the Apex style is pretty.
Do not invent coverage percentages or governor numbers in the review comments.
Do not perform reviews against production customer code in an unauthorized org.

Apex tests in the same sandbox

worked_example.scenario: Interview code-review and design-review exercises: (1) a trigger queries Account inside a for-loop over Opportunities and has no tests; (2) the design stores Legal_Comments__c on Opportunity with OWD Public Read/Write. You have 12 minutes.
inputs: Trigger snippet with SOQL in a loop
Schema sketch with legal text on Opportunity
Author says they will 'add tests later'

decisions.decision: Design-review blocker: legal comments on a public parent fail Trusted/data security; propose a private child or restricted FLS plus OWD change, with Needs verification on exact sharing.
decisions.because: Code review cannot paint over a public legal field.
decisions.rejected: Approving the schema because the trigger names are clean

decisions.decision: Code-review blockers: SOQL in a loop and no tests; nit the variable name only after.
decisions.because: Testing Apex makes tests part of development; bulk-safety is a volume defect.
decisions.rejected: LGTM plus a comment to rename `i`

configuration_or_code: Comment 1 (design): Legal text needs a sharing story; Opportunity public R/W is the wrong occupancy permit.
Comment 2 (code): Query Accounts into a map before the loop.
Comment 3 (code): Add tests with multiple LAB_ Opportunities and an assertion; 'later' is not evidence.
worked_example.output: Two inspections, labeled blockers versus nit, plus a which-tool question if the trigger only stamps a field.
verification: A peer can tell which comments are merge-blocking.
Legal data concern is in design review, not buried as a style note.
worked_example.self_explanation: The candidate used occupancy-permit then punch-list, and did not confuse paint with missing stairs.

hands_on_lab.environment: A sandbox or gist with synthetic LAB_ Apex. No customer production.
starting_state_checks: You have a small trigger or you write a deliberately bad one
steps: Write a deliberately flawed LAB_ trigger: SOQL in a loop, no tests.
Perform a written code-review: two blockers, one question, one nit.
Sketch a design that puts sensitive text on a public object; write a design-review blocker.
Fix the bulk query and add one asserting test; re-review.
Label any remaining comment as nit versus blocker.
guided_completion: Circle comments that would block merge
Name the Well-Architected lens you used
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Review a before-save Flow that should have been a formula; write the which-tool design comment.
evidence: Test method with an assertion on LAB_ data
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete the flawed trigger if it was only for the exercise
hands_on_lab.limitations: Coverage percent rules are Needs verification. Do not copy proprietary client code into the gist.

decision_table.signal: New trigger path with no unit tests
decision_table.choose: Code-review blocker: require asserting tests before merge
decision_table.not: Accept 'we will add tests later' as sufficient
decision_table.why: Testing Apex is part of development; DTD puts tests before deploy

decision_table.signal: SOQL or DML inside a loop over trigger records
decision_table.choose: Code-review blocker: bulk-safe collections; tests with multiple rows
decision_table.not: Nit the loop variable name only
decision_table.why: Volume will fail in production even if one-record demos pass

decision_table.signal: Sensitive text on a widely shared parent object
decision_table.not: Polish Apex getters on the same field
decision_table.why: Well-Architected Trusted/data security is an occupancy-permit issue

decision_table.signal: Trigger only stamps a same-record timestamp
decision_table.choose: Design-review which-tool challenge: formula or before-save Flow may suffice
decision_table.not: Debate brace style on the trigger
decision_table.why: Official which-tool article exists for this smell

decision_table.signal: Rename of a private helper in a well-tested class
decision_table.not: Block the release for the rename
decision_table.why: Paint color is not a missing staircase

limitations: Exact coverage percentages are Needs verification.
CRUD/FLS APIs evolve; ask and look up, do not invent.
security_notes: without sharing plus sensitive fields is a blocker.
Do not paste customer Apex into public gists.
Reviews should ask who can read the data, not only whether it compiles.

troubleshooting.symptom: You ran out of time on naming
check: Did you scan bulk and tests first?
Did you ask a question before a rewrite?

production_notes: Record review outcomes in the PR, not only in the interview room.
Do not merge to production from an unreviewed gist.

interview_questions.question: How do you run a Salesforce code-review exercise?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I scan for tests, bulk-safety, and FLS/sharing first, then label nits. I do not LGTM untested triggers or invent coverage percents.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I say this is a punch list, not a rewrite. Blockers: SOQL in loops, missing asserts, without sharing on sensitive data. I ask volume and users if unclear. I cite Testing Apex as why tests are not optional. Style last.
interview_questions.example: Trigger with query-in-loop: map refactor plus tests with multiple LAB_ Opportunities.

interview_questions.question: How is a design-review exercise different?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I inspect objects, sharing, and which-tool before the Apex style. A public legal field fails even if the code is pretty.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Occupancy permit: is this the right building? Well-Architected Trusted for data security, Easy for maintainability, Adaptable for separation of concerns—each attached to an object. I challenge Apex that a before-save Flow could replace. I do not wait for a CTA-sized board.
interview_questions.example: Move legal comments to a private child object; keep Opportunity freeze declarative.
tradeoffs: When to combine DR and CR
follow_ups: What if they only gave a diff?
What if the schema is already in production?

interview_questions.question: Review this: trigger updates Opportunity in a loop, no tests, great naming.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Two blockers—bulk DML/SOQL pattern and tests—then a labeled nit on names if I have time.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would not praise names first. I describe a 200-record insert failing. I request a map-based query and asserting tests. I ask whether a Flow should have done it. I will not invent governor numbers; I will say volume will hit platform limits.
interview_questions.example: for (Opp o : Trigger.new) { update [select ...]; } — classic review bait.

interview_questions.question: Design: Legal_Comments__c on Opportunity, OWD Public Read/Write. Review it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Design-review blocker on Trusted/data security. I will not code-review the getter until sharing is redesigned.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Anyone who can read Opportunity reads legal comments. I propose a private child or a locked-down field with FLS plus a tighter OWD, and I mark exact sharing as to-be-verified in Setup. Code review of Apex that queries that field would be premature occupancy.
interview_questions.example: Legal_Review__c child, OWD private, owner = legal queue—Needs verification in their org.
weak_answer_warnings: Ignoring sharing because 'it's just a comment field'

interview_questions.question: You spent the whole exercise on import order. Recover.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I name the miss, then spend remaining time on tests, bulk, and sharing.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Interviewers allow recovery. I apologize for inspecting paint. I scan the trigger for loops and tests. I ask one design question if the schema is visible. I leave import order as a labeled nit.
interview_questions.example: Three remaining minutes: 'no tests, SOQL in loop, legal field visibility unknown.'
follow_ups: How do you structure remaining minutes?

interview_questions.question: The author says you are blocking progress. How do you hold a security blocker?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I separate nits from blockers out loud and keep the security item; I offer a thin safe path.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show I am not blocking on names. I explain the occupancy-permit failure. I offer a behind-permission-set field as a temporary control if a child object is too big for the slice—still not public R/W text. I ask what constraint forces speed.
interview_questions.example: Ship FLS-hidden field this sprint; child object next—called out as debt, not as done.
follow_ups: What if legal already emailed the data in Outlook?
weak_answer_warnings: Dropping the blocker to be liked

interview_questions.question: When would you approve Apex in design review instead of sending it back to Flow?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the requirement needs transaction control, complex branching, or a service other Apex must call—after saying why Flow is insufficient.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Which-tool is not 'never Apex.' I approve a service class for multi-object updates with callouts. I still require tests and bulk-safety in code review. I do not approve a timestamp trigger. I mark edition limits Needs verification rather than inventing them.
interview_questions.example: Callout after legal approve is not a validation rule; Apex or an integration tool is in play.
follow_ups: How do you prevent trigger recursion?

interview_questions.question: Teach code-review and design-review with the building-inspection analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Permit then punch list. It breaks because software iterates and paint can be accessibility—but you still do not skip fire exits.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Design review is occupancy: stairs, exits, wiring. Code review is the unit punch list: detectors (tests), wiring load (bulk), locks (FLS). Nits are paint. It breaks when teams ship weekly—security still is not 'later.' Flow still gets a permit. I then give two blocker comments and one nit on a sample trigger.
interview_questions.example: SOQL-in-loop trigger plus public legal field schema.
